With asyncapi the document says AMQP 1.0: the protocol key amqp1, and the crate's facts under the x-ruststream-amqp1 extension.
A subscription's channel reports its address, terminus, credit and settle mode; a publish channel reports the address its sender targets.
A send operation says how it posts: confirmed for Publish, transactional for TransactionalPublish.
A reply reports $message.header#/reply-to as where its address is read, so a transform can answer each request where it asked.
The server reports the host and port with protocol amqp1 and version 1.0, the container id, and never the credentials in the URL.
AmqpBroker connects a service to an AMQP 1.0 broker; new only records the URL, and the runtime connects it once at startup.
container_id names the service to the broker, which is how an operator finds its links in the broker's console; the default is ruststream.
AmqpError is the one error type of the crate: connect, session, attach, publish, receive, request, transaction and a body with no bytes.
One glob, ruststream_amqp::prelude, brings the core prelude, the broker, the descriptor and the policies under Publish and TransactionalPublish.
Sasl picks the authentication: anonymous, plain or external; an amqps:// URL needs the rustls or native-tls feature.
Shutdown ends the subscriptions, the publisher links and the connection in turn; a publisher used afterwards reports NotConnected.
Startup opens the socket, authenticates and begins the publishers' session; a refusal fails the start as AmqpError::Connect.
AmqpPublish, Publish in the prelude, waits for the broker's disposition and reports anything but accepted as PublishNotAccepted.
content-type, correlation-id, reply-to and message-id ride the AMQP properties section; every other header rides application-properties.
The partition-key header rides the AMQP group-id property, and a broker that honours message groups keeps one group on one consumer.
request attaches a dynamic reply link, sends with reply-to and correlation-id, and resolves with the matching reply or RequestTimeout.
A responder reads the private reply address from reply-to and answers there through an injected slot, echoing correlation-id.
A handler's outcome is the delivery's disposition: ack accepts, retry sends modified with delivery-failed, drop rejects.
dead_letter names the address a spent delivery is published to; a cap without one rejects it, and the broker's own dead-letter policy applies.
out_retry(Publish) replaces the registration's retry publisher, and the steps after it, such as a transform, apply to every deferred copy.
max_attempts caps deliveries; the count is the broker's delivery-count, or the framework's header on a copy this crate published.
AMQP 1.0 has no delayed redelivery, so retry_after drops the delivery and publishes a copy to the subscription's own address after the delay.
Settle::AtMostOnce settles each delivery on receipt, so the message is gone whether the handler finished or not, and ack reports Unsupported.
AmqpAddress describes a subscription: the address, the terminus it asks for and its link settings; a bare name sends the address as written.
A slice handler gets the deliveries assembled on the client, up to the size the mount site names, closed early by batch_wait.
credit is the link credit: how many deliveries the broker may send ahead of the handler's settlements, 256 by default and never zero.
AmqpAddress::queue asks for the queue terminus: subscriptions on the address compete, and each message goes to one of them.
AmqpAddress::raw sends the address as written with no capability, for a deployment's own convention such as /queues/orders on RabbitMQ.
AmqpAddress::topic asks for the topic terminus: every subscription on the address gets its own copy of each message.

TestApp::start_live runs the same test body against a running broker, for what only a server has: credit, dead-letter policy, grouping.
TransactionalPublish posts under an AMQP transaction: what a publisher sends between begin and commit becomes visible together, or not at all.

ruststream-amqp 是 RustStream 的 AMQP 1.0 Broker， 基于 fe2o3-amqp 客户端构建。AMQP 1.0 是 ISO 标准，因此一个 crate 即可服务整个协议家族：ActiveMQ Artemis 与 Classic、RabbitMQ 4.x、Azure Service Bus 与 Event Hubs、Amazon MQ、Solace、Apache Qpid 以及 IBM MQ。 在 RabbitMQ 上，AMQP 1.0 与 ruststream-lapin 所用的 AMQP 0.9.1 是两套独立的协议栈。
本节用图说明 AMQP 1.0 如何工作，ruststream-amqp 在 Broker 与 RustStream 运行时之间处于什么位置，以及这给服务带来的开销。

地址指明 Broker 中的一个节点，接收者请求的能力决定它的各个接收者是共用一个队列，还是各得一份副本。 接收者与地址相遇的三种方式：竞争同一个队列、各有一个订阅队列，以及由 Broker 创建的节点消息 1消息 2每条消息每条消息attach地址地址 orders：任播地址 events：组播动态源队列 orders每条消息一次接收者 1能力 queue接收者 2能力 queue接收者 1 的订阅队列接收者 2 的订阅队列接收者 1能力 topic接收者 2能力 topic接收者dynamic = true临时队列由 Broker 命名 以文字阅读本图 地址 orders：任播: 队列 orders 每条消息一次 地址 events：组播: 接收者 1 的 订阅队列; 接收者 2 的 订阅队列 动态源: 接收者 dynamic = true; 临时队列 由 Broker 命名 队列 orders 每条消息一次 → 接收者 1 能力 queue: 消息 1 队列 orders 每条消息一次 → 接收者 2 能力 queue: 消息 2 接收者 1 的 订阅队列 → 接收者 1 能力 topic: 每条消息 接收者 2 的 订阅队列 → 接收者 2 能力 topic: 每条消息 接收者 dynamic = true → 临时队列 由 Broker 命名: attach 临时队列 由 Broker 命名 → 接收者 dynamic = true: 地址 接收者附加时带一个源 terminus：一个节点的地址和一组能力。AmqpAddress::queue 请求能力 queue，AmqpAddress::topic 请求 topic，AmqpAddress::raw 不请求任何能力。 ActiveMQ Artemis 读取这个能力。请求 queue 时，一个地址的各个接收者附加到同一个任播队列并相互竞争：每条消息只交给其中一个。请求 topic 时，地址是组播的，Artemis 为每个接收者各建一个订阅队列，因此每个接收者都收到每条消息。除非 Artemis 的设置禁止，它会在第一次附加时创建地址及其队列；orders::billing 直接指明一个地址下的某个队列。 topic 订阅保留规范规定的 terminus 默认值：不持久，随会话一同过期。它的订阅队列与链路同生共存，因此服务停止期间发布到该主题的消息不会为它保留。 raw 地址原样到达 Broker，由 Broker 自己的配置决定它是什么。其他 Broker 用各自的方式为节点编址：RabbitMQ 4 把队列写作 /queues/orders，把交换器写作 /exchanges/events/key，而且队列必须事先存在。Azure Service Bus 用名称指明队列，把主题订阅写作 events/subscriptions/billing。 接收者可以请求一个动态源，而不是指定源。这时由 Broker 创建一个节点（Artemis 创建临时队列），并在对 attach 的应答中返回它的地址。request 为每次请求附加一个这样的接收者，把地址放进 reply-to 发出，应答到达或超时之后再分离这个接收者。 terminus 的字段来自规范（消息传递，第 3.5 节），地址模型来自 Artemis（AMQP、地址模型）。

AMQP 1.0 事务在 Broker 的协调器上声明，在其下发布的 transfer 要么在提交时一起到达各自的节点，要么都不到达。 事务性发布：在协调器上声明，带 txn-id 发布，再用 discharge 提交或回滚协调器txn-idaccepted或declare在控制器链路上declared协调器的 txn-id发送链路上的 transfer带着 txn-iddischarge fail=false提交accepted：消息一起到达各自的节点dischargefail=true：回滚，什么也不投递discharge 之前，没有消费者能看到在事务中发布的消息 以文字阅读本图 declare 在控制器链路上 → declared 协调器的 txn-id: 协调器 declared 协调器的 txn-id → 发送链路上的 transfer 带着 txn-id: txn-id 发送链路上的 transfer 带着 txn-id → discharge fail=false 提交 discharge fail=false 提交 → accepted： 消息一起到达 各自的节点: accepted 发送链路上的 transfer 带着 txn-id → discharge fail=true： 回滚， 什么也不 投递: 或 discharge 之前，没有消费者能看到 在事务中发布的消息 协调器是 Broker 的一个节点。控制器链路附加到它并发送 declare，协调器用一个事务 id 应答。此后，任何普通发送链路上的 transfer 都在其事务状态中带上这个 id。discharge 结束事务：fail 为 false 时提交，fail 为 true 时回滚。 AmqpTxnPublisher 在事务中发布消息。每次 begin_transaction 在连接的发布者会话上附加一条控制器链路并声明一个事务，commit 和 abort 对它执行 discharge。控制器请求 mixed 发送者结算模式，因为 Artemis 以这种模式应答，而客户端要求 Broker 原样回显它所请求的模式。 各 Broker 在这里有所不同。Artemis 每个会话只服务一个事务，而一个连接的发布者共用一个会话。RabbitMQ 4 不支持 AMQP 1.0 事务。Azure Service Bus 支持它们，并通过 send-via 实体在一个事务中向多个实体发布消息。 协议来自规范（事务），各 Broker 的限制来自各自厂商的文档（Artemis、RabbitMQ、Service Bus）。

ruststream-amqp 如何测量自己：三个循环、在真实 Broker 上的运行、受 Broker 限制的判定计算，以及代码计数。流程就是框架自己的流程（RustStream 方法论），本页说明它在 AMQP 1.0 上是什么样子。

一个进程把场景跑三遍，作为三个循环，它们只有一处不同：承载消息的是什么。 裸客户端。 一个 fe2o3-amqp 接收者，直接驱动：接收、解码、读取一个字段、接受投递。 Broker crate。 本 crate，上面什么也没有：Broker 建立连接，地址描述符打开一个订阅，一个循环从它的流中取出投递、解码并 ack。 RustStream。 用户写的服务：一个 #[subscriber] 处理器及其外围的应用。 其余一切在三个循环中都相同：连接、每条链路所在的会话、256 的链路信用、投递保证、ack 的位置、解码成同一个结构体、载荷字节、带四个工作线程的 tokio 运行时，以及二进制程序。 消息体是 512 字节的 JSON。它解码成一个包含两个整数字段的结构体，因此解码不做内存分配，数字反映的是本 crate，而不是 JSON 解析器。

每次运行使用新的地址。 一次运行永远看不到之前的运行留下的东西。 消费者先附加。 随后，另一个连接上的生产者向它供给消息，最多提前 8192 条。生产者以预先结算的方式发布，因此运行测量的是消费一侧，而不是 Broker 确认一次发送有多快。 在三个循环中，计时窗口都从第一次投递开始，到最后一次投递解码完成时结束。 建立连接、开启会话和附加链路都在窗口之外。 消息条数来自一次探测，它测量裸循环的速率，因此在任何机器上，测量的运行都至少持续五秒。 各循环交替进行：裸、crate、RustStream，共三轮。每个循环报告它最佳、中位和最差的一轮。 当消费者在运行的大部分时间里都在等 Broker 时，该行标为 受 Broker 限制。这是算出来的：一次探测为 20000 次等待 disposition 的发送计时并取中位数，传输说明一次投递需要多少次往返，二者之积达到每条消息测得时间的一半时，该行就被标记。在这里，一次投递不需要往返：Broker 凭客户端在后台补充的信用进行 transfer，接受投递时也不等待应答。往返时间与机器信息一起公布，因此这个计算可以核对。

开销图的每个场景都是用户写的服务，基于 AmqpBroker，连接同一个 Broker，构建时不带 testing 特性，运行在单线程运行时上。一个独立的线程在另一个连接上，于各个测量区间之间填充队列，它的每次发布都等待 Broker 接受。 指令数来自 callgrind，内存分配来自 DHAT。一个场景依次在一次投递、1000 次、2000 次上运行。后两次之差是一条消息的稳态开销，单次投递就是冷启动。 套接字是真实的，所以同一个二进制程序每次运行的计数都会略有变动：一次读取带进多少次 transfer，取决于 Broker 当时已经写出了多少。与保存的基线对照时，某个场景的指令数多出百分之二就算失败。内存分配在每次运行中都受每个场景声明的下限约束，下限是见过的最高计数再加千分之一。

The parts of ruststream-amqp an AMQP 1.0 service uses, one page per component, grouped by the part of the service they belong to. The broker, AmqpBroker, holds the connection. A subscription names its address with a descriptor, and a handler's outcome becomes the delivery's disposition. A service publishes through a policy, asks another service with request-reply, and posts several messages as one transaction. The AMQP bindings describe the service in its AsyncAPI document, and a TestApp test runs it on an in-process transport.

With the asyncapi feature the generated document says AMQP 1.0: the protocol key amqp1, and the crate's facts under the x-ruststream-amqp1 extension. The core builds the AsyncAPI document from the app, before anything connects. The specification has an amqp1 binding, and every one of its objects must stay empty. So this crate writes what it knows into one extension object, x-ruststream-amqp1, at each level where the binding would sit. A server names the protocol and the container the service presents. A channel names its node address and, for a subscription, the link it reads over. A send operation says how it posts. A reply routed per request says where its address is read. Everything comes from the service's own declarations: the broker, the descriptors and the publish policies. The document is published and shared, so no binding carries a credential. The binary #[ruststream::app] writes prints the document with asyncapi gen.

The dependency line: ruststream-amqp = { version = "0.7", features = ["asyncapi"] } The service registers its broker under the label amqp, the key of its server in the document. cargo run --example amqp_asyncapi --features asyncapi,transaction -- asyncapi gen prints the document. A subscription's channel reports its address, terminus, credit and settle mode; a publish channel reports the address its sender targets. A subscription's extension has four fields, read from its AmqpAddress. address is the node the receiver attaches to. capability is the terminus it asks for, queue or topic. An AmqpAddress::raw address asks for none, so its channel has no capability. credit is the link credit, 256 unless the descriptor sets credit. settleMode is at-least-once, or at-most-once for a descriptor with Settle::AtMostOnce. A channel the service publishes to carries one field, address: the node the sender attaches its target to. That is a reply destination, the name of an Out slot, or a dead-letter address. A reply routed per request has no fixed address on its channel, and the extension still names the destination its mount site declared.

The channel orders reports a queue with a credit of 64, events a topic settled at most once, and /queues/audit no terminus. The channels receipts, orders.dead and ledger report the address each sender targets. Macros Manual examples/amqp_asyncapi.rs #[subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue("orders").credit(nonzero!(64)), reply("receipts"))] async fn confirm(order: &Order) -> Receipt { Receipt { order_id: order.id } } #[subscriber(AmqpAddress::topic("events").settle(Settle::AtMostOnce))] async fn watch(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "event seen"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[subscriber(AmqpAddress::raw("/queues/audit"))] async fn audit(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "audited"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } examples/manual/amqp_asyncapi.rs /// The queue `orders`, with a credit of 64. fn orders() -> AmqpAddress { AmqpAddress::queue("orders").credit(nonzero!(64)) } /// The topic `events`, settled on receipt. fn events() -> AmqpAddress { AmqpAddress::topic("events").settle(Settle::AtMostOnce) } /// The address `/queues/audit`, sent as written. fn audit_queue() -> AmqpAddress { AmqpAddress::raw("/queues/audit") }

A send operation says how it posts: confirmed for Publish, transactional for TransactionalPublish. The extension of a send operation has one field, posting, and the publish policy at its mount site decides it. Publish posts confirmed: each transfer waits for the broker's outcome, and anything but accepted fails the publish. TransactionalPublish posts transactional: the transfers carry a transaction and become visible at its commit. A dead-letter destination has a send operation of its own, and it posts confirmed. A reply has no send operation. What a reply policy adds to the document is on its reply.

The operation send_events_orders_dead posts confirmed, and send_payments_ledger posts transactional. A reply reports $message.header#/reply-to as where its address is read, so a transform can answer each request where it asked. A request on this broker sets the AMQP reply-to property, and a handler reads it as the reply-to header. A reply can follow it: a transform on out_reply that declares Destination = Names sets the reply's address from that header. The reply then has no fixed address, and the receive operation's reply says where a client reads it: $message.header#/reply-to. Both publish policies report that location. The mount site still names a reply destination, such as reply("receipts"). It is the reply's declared channel, and a delivery the transform leaves alone, one without reply-to, is answered there.

The reply of receive_orders reports its address location as $message.header#/reply-to. Macros Manual examples/amqp_asyncapi.rs /// The receipt names no address of its own, so the transform may name one per delivery. #[derive(Debug, Serialize, Outgoing)] struct Receipt { order_id: u64, } /// Answers where the request asked to be answered: the `reply-to` property, which a handler reads /// as the `reply-to` header. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)] struct ToReplyTo; impl<C, Options> PublishTransform<ForReply<C>, Options> for ToReplyTo { type Destination = Names; fn apply( &self, out: &mut Outgoing<'_>, _options: &mut Option<Options>, cx: &PublishContext<'_, C>, ) { if let Some(address) = cx.headers().get_str("reply-to") { let address = address.to_owned(); out.set_name(address); } } } examples/manual/amqp_asyncapi.rs /// The receipt names no address of its own, so the transform may name one per delivery. #[derive(Debug, Serialize, Outgoing, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Receipt { order_id: u64, } /// Answers where the request asked to be answered: the `reply-to` property, which a handler reads /// as the `reply-to` header. #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)] struct ToReplyTo; impl<C, Options> PublishTransform<ForReply<C>, Options> for ToReplyTo { type Destination = Names; fn apply( &self, out: &mut Outgoing<'_>, _options: &mut Option<Options>, cx: &PublishContext<'_, C>, ) { if let Some(address) = cx.headers().get_str("reply-to") { let address = address.to_owned(); out.set_name(address); } } }

The server reports the host and port with protocol amqp1 and version 1.0, the container id, and never the credentials in the URL. A broker registered with with_broker_labeled is a server of the document, under its label. Its host is the host and port of the broker's URL. The user and the password the URL carries stay out of it. The protocol is amqp1, and protocolVersion is 1.0. The specification's key amqp means AMQP 0.9.1, and both protocols use the amqp:// scheme and port 5672. The key and the version tell a reader, or a tool that generates a client, which protocol the service speaks. The extension carries containerId, the name the service presents on the connection. It is the broker's container_id, ruststream when the service sets none. An operator finds the service's links by that name in the broker's console.

The broker's URL carries a password, and the server in the document is broker.example.com:5672 with the container billing-svc. Macros Manual examples/amqp_asyncapi.rs /// The production broker. The password rides the URL, and the document reports the host alone. fn broker(password: &str) -> AmqpBroker { AmqpBroker::new(format!("amqp://billing:{password}@broker.example.com:5672")) .container_id("billing-svc") } examples/manual/amqp_asyncapi.rs /// The production broker. AmqpBroker connects a service to an AMQP 1.0 broker; new only records the URL, and the runtime connects it once at startup. AMQP 1.0 is an ISO standard, so one broker type serves ActiveMQ Artemis and Classic, RabbitMQ 4.x, Azure Service Bus, Amazon MQ, Solace, Apache Qpid and IBM MQ. AmqpBroker::new takes the broker's URL: amqp://host:port, or amqps://host:port for TLS. A URL without a port uses 5672 for amqp and 5671 for amqps. The constructor does no I/O, so the whole service fits the synchronous #[ruststream::app] builder. The settings that follow it are builder steps too: the authentication and the container id. At startup the runtime connects the broker and receives a ConnectedAmqpBroker. The connect opens the socket, authenticates and opens the AMQP connection, so a broker that is unreachable or refuses the service fails startup instead of the first publish. Every subscription and every publisher of the service runs on that one connection. At shutdown the runtime closes the connection, and the connected form is consumed with it. #[subscriber("orders")] opens the address orders as it is written, without a terminus capability. The broker's own configuration then decides whether the subscriptions on the address compete or each get a copy. AmqpAddress::queue and AmqpAddress::topic state that choice in the service; the Subscriptions pages describe them. Getting started runs a first service against a local ActiveMQ Artemis.

The service reads the queue address orders. cargo run --example amqp_service --features testing -- run starts it against a broker on localhost:5672 with the user artemis. Macros Manual examples/amqp_service.rs use ruststream_amqp::prelude::*; #[subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue("orders"))] async fn place(order: &Order) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(order.id, "order placed"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( AmqpBroker::new("amqp://artemis:artemis@localhost:5672"), |b| { b.include(place); }, ) } examples/manual/amqp_service.rs use ruststream_amqp::prelude::*; struct Place; impl Handle<Order> for Place { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order placed"); ready(Ok(())) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( AmqpBroker::new("amqp://artemis:artemis@localhost:5672"), |b| { let place = subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue("orders"), Place); b.include(place.build()); }, ) }

container_id names the service to the broker, which is how an operator finds its links in the broker's console; the default is ruststream. Every AMQP 1.0 connection opens with a container id, the name of the process on each end. Each link the service attaches takes its name from it, with a role and a number that keeps the name unique on the connection: Link Name a subscription's receiver <container>-receiver-<n> a publisher's sender, one per address <container>-sender-<n> the reply link of a request <container>-reply-<n> the controller of a transaction <container>-txn-<n> The generated AsyncAPI document reports the container id beside the server's host and port, in the x-ruststream-amqp1 extension.

The service presents itself to the broker as orders-svc. Macros Manual examples/amqp_broker_container.rs /// The broker, which knows this service as `orders-svc`. fn broker() -> AmqpBroker { AmqpBroker::new("amqp://artemis:artemis@broker.internal:5672").container_id("orders-svc") } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker(), |b| { b.include(place); }) } examples/manual/amqp_broker_container.rs /// The broker, which knows this service as `orders-svc`. fn broker() -> AmqpBroker { AmqpBroker::new("amqp://artemis:artemis@broker.internal:5672").container_id("orders-svc") } fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker(), |b| { let place = subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue("orders"), Place); b.include(place.build()); }) }

AmqpError is the one error type of the crate: connect, session, attach, publish, receive, request, transaction and a body with no bytes. Each variant names the step that failed. The client's error behind it is its source, so the fe2o3-amqp types stay out of the crate's API. Variant When Connect the URL, the socket, TLS, the login or the AMQP open failed, or the connection failed to close at shutdown Session the broker refused a session, the publishers' or a subscription's Attach the broker refused a link: a subscription's receiver, a publisher's sender, a request's reply link Detach a link failed to close at shutdown Publish the connection failed while a message was sent PublishNotAccepted the broker settled a published message as rejected, released or modified, so the message is not on the broker Receive the connection failed while a subscription received UnsupportedBody a delivery's body is an AMQP value that is neither binary nor a string; the delivery is rejected, and the runtime logs the error RequestTimeout a request had no reply within its timeout NotConnected a publisher, a subscription or a transaction was used before the connect or after the shutdown InvalidAddress a subscription's address is empty Transaction a transaction step was called in a state that cannot serve it (transaction feature) A service meets the error in two places. A failed startup carries it as a source of the runtime's error, and the service exits before it reads anything. A publish from a handler returns it as the source of the core's PublishError, and the handler decides how the delivery settles. The enum is #[non_exhaustive], so a match on it ends with a wildcard arm.

The handler sends each shipment to the warehouse address its order names. A shipment the broker refuses drops the order, since sending it again meets the same answer; any other failure retries it. Macros Manual examples/amqp_broker_errors.rs #[subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue("orders"))] async fn ship(order: &Order, Out(warehouses): Out<impl Publisher>) -> HandlerOutcome { let shipment = Shipment { order_id: order.id }; let sent = warehouses .message(&shipment) .to(order.warehouse.as_str()) .publish() .await; match sent { Ok(()) => HandlerOutcome::ack(), Err(err) => { tracing::warn!(subscription = "orders", order.id, error = %err, "shipment not sent"); if refused_by_the_broker(&err) { HandlerOutcome::drop() } else { HandlerOutcome::retry() } } } } /// Whether the broker settled the message with an outcome other than accepted. Sending it again /// meets the same answer, while a connection that failed under the publish may be back by the next /// attempt. fn refused_by_the_broker(err: &(dyn Error + 'static)) -> bool { let mut cause = Some(err); while let Some(err) = cause { if let Some(AmqpError::PublishNotAccepted { .. }) = err.downcast_ref() { return true; } cause = err.source(); } false } examples/manual/amqp_broker_errors.rs struct Ship; impl<Entry> Handle<Order, (), Outs<(Entry,)>> for Ship where Entry: OutEntry<DefaultSlot, Wire: Publisher>, { async fn handle( &self, order: &Order, outs: &Outs<(Entry,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let shipment = Shipment { order_id: order.id }; let sent = outs .get(DefaultSlot) .message(&shipment) .to(order.warehouse.as_str()) .publish() .await; if let Err(err) = sent { tracing::warn!(subscription = "orders", order.id, error = %err, "shipment not sent"); if refused_by_the_broker(&err) { return Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()); } return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()); } Ok(()) } } /// Whether the broker settled the message with an outcome other than accepted. Sending it again /// meets the same answer, while a connection that failed under the publish may be back by the next /// attempt. fn refused_by_the_broker(err: &(dyn Error + 'static)) -> bool { let mut cause = Some(err); while let Some(err) = cause { if let Some(AmqpError::PublishNotAccepted { .. }) = err.downcast_ref() { return true; } cause = err.source(); } false }

One glob, ruststream_amqp::prelude, brings the core prelude, the broker, the descriptor and the policies under Publish and TransactionalPublish. use ruststream_amqp::prelude::*; is the one import an AMQP 1.0 service writes. It carries the core's own prelude, so #[subscriber], RustStream, HandlerOutcome, Out and nonzero! come with it. It adds AmqpBroker with its authentication Sasl, the address descriptor AmqpAddress with its delivery guarantee Settle, the crate's error AmqpError, and the capability trait RequestReply. The publish policies come under the names every broker crate uses: Publish is AmqpPublish, and with the transaction feature TransactionalPublish is AmqpTransactionalPublish, next to the capability trait TransactionalPublisher. So a mount site reads the same on every broker. Two broker preludes in one file collide on these names; the prefixed originals, exported here too, tell them apart. A handler body bounds its slots with capability traits, such as Out<impl Publisher> or Out<impl RequestReply>, and names no broker type. A service that reads a delivery's partition key through the Partitioned capability imports ruststream::Partitioned itself. In the glob it would make partition_key() ambiguous with the method of the same name that the core prelude brings.

The broker, its authentication, the descriptor with its settings and the reply policy all come from the one glob. Macros Manual examples/amqp_broker_prelude.rs use ruststream_amqp::prelude::*; #[subscriber( AmqpAddress::queue("orders") .credit(nonzero!(64)) .settle(Settle::AtLeastOnce), reply )] async fn confirm(order: &Order) -> Confirmation { Confirmation { id: order.id } } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( AmqpBroker::new("amqp://broker.internal:5672").sasl(Sasl::anonymous()), |b| { b.include(confirm).out_reply(Publish); }, ) } examples/manual/amqp_broker_prelude.rs use ruststream_amqp::prelude::*; struct Confirm; impl Handle<Order, Confirmation> for Confirm { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<Confirmation, HandlerOutcome>> { ready(Ok(Confirmation { id: order.id })) } } fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( AmqpBroker::new("amqp://broker.internal:5672").sasl(Sasl::anonymous()), |b| { let confirm = subscriber( AmqpAddress::queue("orders") .credit(nonzero!(64)) .settle(Settle::AtLeastOnce), Confirm, ); b.include(confirm.reply().build()).out_reply(Publish); }, ) }

Sasl picks the authentication: anonymous, plain or external; an amqps:// URL needs the rustls or native-tls feature. A service logs in one of two ways, and a broker uses one of them. Credentials in the URL, amqp://user:password@host, log in with SASL PLAIN. A profile set with sasl goes with a URL that carries no credentials: Profile Login Sasl::plain(user, password) SASL PLAIN with the user and password as written Sasl::anonymous() SASL ANONYMOUS, for a broker that admits clients without credentials Sasl::external() SASL EXTERNAL: the broker takes an identity established outside SASL; it needs an amqps:// URL A password the deployment hands the service, from the environment or a secret store, goes through Sasl::plain. So does a password with a character the URL reserves, such as @, :, / or %. A connection with neither credentials nor a profile opens without SASL, and a broker that requires a login refuses it. A refused login, such as a wrong password, and Sasl::external on an amqp:// URL fail startup with AmqpError::Connect. An amqps:// URL encrypts the connection with TLS. The rustls feature checks the broker's certificate against the Mozilla root certificates built into the binary. The native-tls feature uses the operating system's TLS library and its trust store; with both features enabled, native-tls is the one used. The connect checks the certificate against the host in the URL, so the URL names the broker by a host name or an IPv4 address. An IPv6 address gives TLS no server name, so the connect fails on it. The connection presents no client certificate. A TestApp test reads the URL as the connect reads it, so an amqps:// URL without a TLS feature fails startup there too. The login itself happens only against a broker, in a live test. The generated AsyncAPI document reports the host and port and never the credentials in the URL. Connecting to production takes the URL and the credentials from the environment.

The dependency line: ruststream-amqp = { version = "0.7", features = ["rustls"] } The service logs in as orders-svc over TLS. The password comes from the environment. Shutdown ends the subscriptions, the publisher links and the connection in turn; a publisher used afterwards reports AmqpError::NotConnected. When shutdown begins, the runtime stops reading and waits for the handlers still running. The app's shutdown_timeout bounds that wait; without it the runtime waits until every handler has finished. A publish returns once the broker has settled the message, so what the handlers published is on the broker by then, and nothing is left to send. The broker then closes from the inside out: each subscription's session ends, the publishers' sender links detach, their shared session ends, and the connection closes. Each layer still has to carry the broker's answer to the layer inside it, which fixes the order. The connection closes only after every subscription's session has ended, the sessions of subscriptions still open at shutdown included, so a clean stop reports no error. Every step runs even after an earlier one fails, so a stuck link cannot leave the connection open. The shutdown reports the first failure in that order: AmqpError::Detach for a link, AmqpError::Session for the session, AmqpError::Connect for the connection. A publisher taken before the shutdown keeps pointing at the closed connection. A publish through it, or a transaction begun on a transactional publisher, returns AmqpError::NotConnected and never succeeds against the dead connection. A delivery settled after the shutdown reports an error, and the stream of a subscription that was still open ends.

Handlers still running at shutdown get ten seconds to finish before the broker closes. Macros Manual examples/amqp_broker_shutdown.rs /// The service on `broker`. Once shutdown begins, the handlers still running get ten seconds to /// finish before the broker closes. fn service(broker: AmqpBroker) -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(place); }) .shutdown_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10)) } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { service(AmqpBroker::new("amqp://artemis:artemis@localhost:5672")) } examples/manual/amqp_broker_shutdown.rs /// The service on `broker`. Once shutdown begins, the handlers still running get ten seconds to /// finish before the broker closes. fn service(broker: AmqpBroker) -> impl App<State = ()> { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")) .with_broker(broker, |b| { let place = subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue(orders()), Place); b.include(place.build()); }) .shutdown_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10)) } fn app() -> impl App<State = ()> { service(AmqpBroker::new("amqp://artemis:artemis@localhost:5672")) }

Startup opens the socket, authenticates and begins the publishers' session; a refusal fails the start as AmqpError::Connect. The runtime connects the broker once, before any handler runs. The connect opens a TCP socket to the URL's host with Nagle's algorithm off: AMQP sends a small frame and waits for the answer, which that algorithm would hold back. Over the socket it runs TLS for an amqps:// URL, the SASL login, and the AMQP open with the service's container id. It then begins one session that every publisher of the service shares. A failure of the socket, TLS, the login or the open fails startup with AmqpError::Connect, and a session the broker refuses with AmqpError::Session. The service exits before it reads anything. Each subscription then begins a session of its own and attaches a receiver link to its address. AMQP counts flow control per session, so a slow subscription holds back neither the publishers nor another subscription. An attach the broker refuses fails startup with AmqpError::Attach, which names the address. An empty address fails with AmqpError::InvalidAddress before any I/O. A publisher attaches its sender link to an address on the first publish there, and every later publish to the address reuses that link. A TestApp test connects in process and reads the URL as the connect reads it. A scheme other than amqp or amqps, a URL without a host, or amqps without a TLS feature fails startup in a test as in production. A refused socket or login happens only against a broker, in a live test.

The deployment names the broker in AMQP_URL, credentials included. AmqpPublish, Publish in the prelude, waits for the broker's disposition and reports anything but accepted as PublishNotAccepted. The policy has no fields, so a mount site writes it bare. It is named wherever a registration publishes: .out_reply(Publish) for a reply, .out(Slot, Publish).build() for a slot, .out_retry(Publish) for retry copies. The policy holds no connection; the runtime pairs it with the connected broker at startup into an AmqpPublisher. It is also the broker's default policy, so a reply registration that names no policy publishes through it. The publishers share one AMQP session. A sender link is attached to an address on its first publish and kept for the next ones. Each publish waits for the broker's outcome of the transfer. An accepted outcome completes it; rejected, released or modified fails it with the address and the outcome, so a refusal never passes as sent. The message carries the encoded value as one data section. Headers ride the message's properties and application-properties sections, and the partition key rides group-id. A publish carries no per-message settings: the message goes out without the header section, so it is not durable and keeps the default priority and no time to live. Where a reply goes is a property of its type: #[outgoing(name = "receipts")] fixes the address. A reply to an address the request names is the request-reply pattern.

content-type, correlation-id, reply-to and message-id ride the AMQP properties section; every other header rides application-properties. The crate adds no envelope of its own, so a peer that does not use RustStream reads a plain AMQP message. On publish each well-known header fills the property of the same name. The partition key fills group-id. Any other header becomes an application property: a UTF-8 value as a string, any other value as binary. On delivery a handler reads both sections as one header map, through ctx.headers(). correlation_id() and reply_to() read the two properties request-reply uses. A message id or a correlation id the sender wrote as a UUID, a number or binary reads as text. An application property the sender wrote as a number, a boolean or a timestamp reads as text too; a timestamp reads as milliseconds. A message type declares its headers with #[outgoing(headers = ..)], and a field renamed to correlation-id lands in the property. A HeaderMap with the same entries works the same. The in-process mode frames a publish through the same mapping, so a test reads the headers a live delivery carries.

The partition-key header, PARTITION_KEY_HEADER, rides the AMQP group-id property, and a broker that honours message groups keeps one group on one consumer. The header is named partition-key, the name the in-memory broker uses, so a service keeps its headers when it changes brokers. On publish its value becomes the message's group-id and does not travel as an application property. On delivery group-id comes back as the partition-key header. Message groups are the broker's feature. On ActiveMQ Artemis every message of one group goes to one consumer of the queue, so the consumer sees the group in the order it was sent. Competing consumers of an AmqpAddress::queue address then share the groups instead of the messages. A message type declares the header with #[outgoing(headers = ..)] and a field renamed to partition-key; a HeaderMap with that entry works the same. In process the key travels as on a server, and the consumers of a queue take turns whatever the group. Pinning a group to one consumer is the server's work, so a running broker is where it shows.

request attaches a dynamic reply link, sends with reply-to and correlation-id, and resolves with the matching reply or RequestTimeout. Request-reply is part of AMQP 1.0, and AmqpPublisher implements the RequestReply capability. A request attaches a receiver link with a dynamic source, and the broker names a private address for that link. The message goes out with that address in reply-to and a fresh id in correlation-id. The call resolves with the first message on the link whose correlation-id matches, so a late answer to an earlier request is ignored. With no match inside the timeout the call returns RequestTimeout. The reply link is detached either way, so each request costs a link attach and a detach on top of the two messages. A handler asks through a slot it binds as Out<impl RequestReply>. The mount site gives the slot the plain policy: .out(DefaultSlot, Publish).build(). The reply arrives already settled; the handler reads its payload and headers. A request that opens a conversation has no delivery to answer, so it runs from after_startup, where the publisher is already live. The other side of the exchange is a responder. Request-reply asks a pricing service for the price of each order.

A responder reads the private reply address from reply-to and answers there through an injected slot, echoing correlation-id. The reply address is new for every request, so neither the reply type nor the mount site can name it. The handler reads it with ctx.headers().reply_to() and publishes with .to(reply_to) at the call site. That call site exists only for a reply type whose Outgoing derive names no destination. The slot is bound as Out<impl Publisher> and mounted with .out(DefaultSlot, Publish).build(). The answer copies the request's correlation-id, which ctx.headers().correlation_id() reads. A requester matches the answer by that id, and an answer without it never resolves the request, which then times out. A message without reply-to is no request; the example drops it, which rejects the delivery. A request whose payload is plain bytes reads them through a Deserialized type and answers with a Serialized one, so no codec touches either side.

A handler's outcome is the delivery's disposition: ack accepts, retry sends modified with delivery-failed, drop rejects. In AMQP 1.0 a receiver settles each delivery with a disposition, and the broker acts on its outcome. ack sends accepted, and the broker forgets the message. retry sends modified with delivery-failed set and undeliverable-here cleared. The broker adds the failed attempt to the message's delivery-count and delivers it again, to this subscription or to another receiver on the address. A retry never sends released: that outcome says the delivery was not acted on, so the broker leaves the count as it was, and a cap on the attempts reads that count. drop sends rejected, which ends the delivery: the broker's dead-letter policy decides where it goes, and ActiveMQ Artemis moves it to its DLQ address by default. A delivery that is never settled, because the process stopped, stays on its link until the link detaches, and the broker then hands it to the next receiver. AMQP 1.0 has no delayed redelivery, so retry_after is the runtime's own copy. Under Settle::AtMostOnce the delivery is settled on receipt, and the outcome reaches no broker. In process, TestApp keeps the same rules: a retry comes back with one more counted attempt, and a drop removes the delivery. Acknowledgement and delivery guarantees settles the deliveries of a warehouse.

dead_letter(address) names the address a spent delivery is published to; a cap without one rejects it, and the broker's own dead-letter policy applies. It follows max_attempts(n) at the mount site. When the delivery that fails is the n-th one, the runtime rejects it and publishes a copy to the dead-letter address instead of the subscription's. The copy keeps the payload and the headers, and RETRY_COUNT_HEADER on it says how many times the message was delivered. It leaves through the registration's retry publisher, so the steps that follow out_retry apply to it too. The dead-letter address is an ordinary address: a subscription of this service, or of another one, reads it. A cap without dead_letter rejects the spent delivery, and a warning names the subscription. Where a rejected delivery goes is the broker's policy: ActiveMQ Artemis moves it to its DLQ address by default. The original of a dead-letter copy is rejected as well, so on Artemis the spent delivery also reaches DLQ. In process a rejected delivery leaves the transport, so a test asserts the copy on the named address, as the example's test does. Retries and dead letters reads the dead letters of a refunds service.

The transform declares Destination = Reads: the copy goes where the runtime sends it, and a transform that declares Names does not compile on this position. max_attempts(n) caps deliveries; the count is the broker's delivery-count, or the framework's header on a copy this crate published. The cap counts the deliveries of one message at the mount site, the first one included. A delivery whose message carries the AMQP header section reports the broker's delivery-count, which every retry increments. A message this crate published carries no header section, so the broker has counted nothing for it, and the count is RETRY_COUNT_HEADER instead. Under a cap, a retry of such a message is the runtime's copy, not the broker's redelivery: the runtime rejects the delivery and publishes it again to the subscription's address at once, with the header incremented. A delivery that reaches the cap is not retried: it goes to the dead-letter address, or is rejected where the registration names none. A retry on a registration with no cap stays the broker's own redelivery, and nothing limits it. The runtime rejects every original it replaces with a copy, so a broker that dead-letters rejected deliveries keeps those originals: ActiveMQ Artemis moves them to its DLQ address by default. The copies leave through the retry publisher of the registration. Retries and dead letters caps the attempts of a refunds service.

AMQP 1.0 has no delayed redelivery, so retry_after(delay) drops the delivery and publishes a copy to the subscription's own address after the delay. The runtime rejects the delivery, waits out the delay and publishes a copy of the message, payload and headers, with RETRY_COUNT_HEADER incremented. The copy goes to the subscription's address, because one AMQP node is both what a receiver attaches to and what a sender publishes to, so the mount site names no destination. A bare name and every descriptor answer the same way. On a queue the copy competes for the receivers like any other message. On a topic every subscription on the address receives the copy, not only the one that asked for it. The copy waits in the service's memory, so the retry is at-most-once over the delay: a process that stops before the timer fires loses it. The rejected original is the broker's to handle: ActiveMQ Artemis moves it to its DLQ address by default, beside the copy that comes back. A cap reads the header of the copy, so it holds across delays. In a test the delay runs on the test's clock: tb.advance(delay) brings the copy back.

Settle::AtMostOnce settles each delivery on receipt, so the message is gone whether the handler finished or not, and ack reports Unsupported. AmqpAddress::settle sets the mode on the descriptor. Settle::AtLeastOnce is the default: the handler's outcome settles the delivery, as Dispositions describes. Settle::AtMostOnce accepts each delivery as it arrives, before the handler runs. The broker forgets the message at once, so a crash in the middle of the handler, a retry or a drop brings nothing back. The outcome the handler returns has nothing left to settle: the settlement reports AckError::Unsupported, and the runtime logs a warning that names the subscription. The mode suits traffic where a lost message costs less than a redelivered one, such as a reading that a sensor sends again a second later. The credit of an at-most-once subscription tops itself up as the deliveries arrive. In process, TestApp settles on receipt the same way, so a test sees a retry bring nothing back.

AmqpAddress describes a subscription: the address, the terminus it asks for and its link settings; a bare name sends the address as written. #[subscriber("orders")] opens a receiver on the address orders. The name reaches the broker as written, with no terminus capability, which makes it the same subscription as AmqpAddress::raw. AMQP 1.0 standardises the wire, not what an address means, so whether the subscriptions on one address compete or each get a copy is a question the broker answers. A descriptor asks the question explicitly: AmqpAddress::queue asks for competing consumers, AmqpAddress::topic for a copy each. A descriptor goes where the name goes, as the attribute's first argument. It also carries the link settings: the credit, the settle mode and the deadline of a batch. The manual form passes either one to subscriber(source, body) as its first argument. The subscription's name is its address: a test reads its deliveries under that name, and a deferred retry is published back to it. An empty address stops the service at startup with AmqpError::InvalidAddress. Queues and topics builds a service on a work queue, a broadcast and a raw address.

A slice handler gets the deliveries assembled on the client, up to the size the mount site names, closed early by batch_wait. A handler over &[T] is a batch handler, and batch(n) at the mount site is its largest batch. AMQP 1.0 transfers one message at a time, and credit is flow control rather than a batch size, so the subscription assembles the batches itself. A batch closes when it holds n deliveries, or when batch_wait has passed since its first delivery. The default, DEFAULT_BATCH_WAIT, is 10 ms. A longer wait fills batches under a trickle of traffic, at the cost of latency for the first delivery of each batch. batch_wait applies to batch handlers only: a single-message subscription hands every delivery over as it arrives. One outcome settles every delivery of the batch, and a Vec<HandlerOutcome> settles delivery i with outcome i. In the manual form the body is an impl Handle<[T]>, where Ok(()) acks the batch and Err(outcomes) settles it delivery by delivery. Acknowledgement and delivery guarantees restocks a warehouse from batches.

AmqpAddress::credit sets the link credit: how many deliveries the broker may send ahead of the handler's settlements, 256 by default and never zero. AMQP 1.0 has flow control instead of a prefetch count: a receiver grants credit, and the broker sends a delivery only while it holds some. The subscription grants the full credit when it attaches. Each time half of the credit has been settled, it grants the full credit again, counted from the last delivery the broker sent. So the broker never runs more than credit deliveries ahead of the last grant, but the deliveries held unsettled can outnumber the credit. With a credit of 4, the second settlement brings four more deliveries while two are still open: six unsettled on a credit of four. The default, DEFAULT_CREDIT, is 256, and its first top-up comes after 128 settlements. On a queue, a lower credit spreads a backlog across more replicas, and a higher one keeps a fast handler busy. Under at-most-once every delivery is settled as it arrives, so the credit tops itself up without waiting for the handler. The credit is a NonZeroU32: credit(nonzero!(0)) does not compile, because a receiver with no credit receives nothing. Credit is a property of the link, which only a broker has: in process, TestApp hands every delivery over at once, and the example's live test holds the window to what a broker does.

AmqpAddress::queue asks for the queue terminus: subscriptions on the address compete, and each message goes to one of them. The descriptor attaches its receiver with the terminus capability queue on the link's source. ActiveMQ Artemis and the other brokers that read the capability treat the address as anycast. That is a work queue: two replicas of a service share the orders, and no order is handled twice. A delivery handed back with a retry goes to whichever receiver the broker picks next. Once a queue subscription has attached, the queue keeps what is published while no receiver is attached, so a replica that restarts finds its backlog. A delivery the process held unsettled when it stopped returns to the queue as well. In process, TestApp hands the messages of a queue address to its subscriptions in turn, as the example's test shows with two replicas.

AmqpAddress::raw sends the address as written with no capability, for a deployment's own convention such as /queues/orders on RabbitMQ. RabbitMQ 4.x addresses a queue by its v2 path, /queues/<name>, and ActiveMQ Artemis accepts a fully qualified queue name. A bare name in #[subscriber("orders")] is a raw address too. With no capability on the link, the broker's own configuration decides whether the subscriptions on the address compete or each get a copy. The address is matched exactly: orders and /queues/orders are two different nodes. In process, TestApp delivers each message of a raw address once, as on a queue, because there is no broker configuration to consult. TestApp::start connects AmqpBroker in process: queues, topics, dispositions, request-reply and transactions, with no broker running. A test hands the harness the app main runs, unchanged, and addresses the broker by its production type, tb.broker::<AmqpBroker>(). The testing feature in [dev-dependencies] adds the in-process mode, and turns on the core's harness with it. The connected broker then carries an in-process transport in place of the connection, and so do its subscribers, its publishers and its deliveries. The descriptors and publish policies of the service are the production ones. The transport has no settings of its own. It reads the broker's URL as the connect reads it, and frames a publish with the same AMQP sections a live publish goes through, so a handler reads the headers a live delivery carries. It routes by the exact address, as a broker does. Subscriptions on a queue address compete, one delivery each, and every topic subscription gets a copy. A raw address is delivered once, like a queue; a test that asserts a broadcast subscribes with topic. A queue subscription creates its address's queue, and a message published while no consumer is attached waits there for the next one. The disposition of a handler's outcome behaves as on a broker: a retry comes back with its delivery-count one higher, a drop rejects, and an at-most-once delivery arrives settled. Batches, requests with their reply address and timeout, and transactions work as they do live. The transport refuses what a broker refuses. A message to the empty address is rejected, and a publisher, a subscription, a settlement or a transaction used after shutdown fails with the error a live connection returns. A publish through the harness returns once every handler it woke has settled, so the assertions that follow read finished state. What only a broker has, such as link credit, the dead-letter policy behind a rejection, message groups and the login, is for a live test. Testing an AMQP service tests a payments service in process and against a broker.

It connects the broker through its ordinary connect, so the socket, the login and every subscription's link are real. The body is the one an in-process test runs; only the start call differs. A publish, settle and advance wait on the real clock until every subscription has handled what was published to it. The wait lasts ten seconds at most, and start_live_within sets another bound. A broker keeps what earlier runs left on it. Each run reads addresses of its own, named with the process id, so it never takes a message an earlier run left behind. AmqpTransactionalPublish, TransactionalPublish in the prelude, posts under an AMQP transaction: what a publisher sends between begin and commit becomes visible together, or not at all. The policy needs the transaction feature. The runtime pairs it into an AmqpTxnPublisher, which implements TransactionalPublisher. A handler binds its slot as Out<impl TransactionalPublisher>, and the mount site names the policy with .out(DefaultSlot, TransactionalPublish).build(). begin_transaction declares a transaction on the broker. Each publish after it is posted under that transaction and waits for the broker's outcome, as a plain publish does. commit makes every posted message visible at once; abort discards them. A publish with no transaction open goes out at once. The handle holds one transaction at a time. A second begin_transaction while one is open fails and leaves the open one untouched. commit or abort with nothing open fails too. A commit or an abort that fails has still ended the transaction, so the next begin_transaction starts a new one. Each failure is an AmqpError::Transaction. The slot's publisher is paired once, at startup, so every delivery of the registration uses the same handle. A registration that runs deliveries side by side with workers(n) has them compete for the one transaction, and a second begin_transaction fails until the first ends. A transaction covers what the publisher posts. The delivery the handler answers settles on its own after the handler returns, so a delivery redelivered after a commit posts its messages again. Transactions bills an order with its ledger entries and invoice in one transaction.

本指南结算投递，限定尝试次数，按至多一次读取队列，设定链路信用，并处理批。 在 AMQP 1.0 中，接收者用一个结果结算每次投递，Broker 据此行动。 处理器的结果就是这个 disposition。 示例是一个仓库。 它拣选货件，记录每次拣选，并用成批到达的投递补充货架。

宏 手写 src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize)] struct Shipment { id: u64, sku: String, quantity: u32, } /// The goods the warehouse has on its shelves. fn in_stock(sku: &str) -> bool { matches!(sku, "book" | "pen") } #[subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue("shipments").credit(nonzero!(32)))] async fn pick(shipment: &Shipment) -> HandlerOutcome { if shipment.quantity == 0 { tracing::warn!(shipment.id, "an empty shipment rejected"); return HandlerOutcome::drop(); } if !in_stock(&shipment.sku) { tracing::info!( shipment.id, shipment.sku, "out of stock, the shipment comes back" ); return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } tracing::info!(shipment.id, shipment.sku, "shipment picked"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Shipment { id: u64, sku: String, quantity: u32, } /// The goods the warehouse has on its shelves. fn in_stock(sku: &str) -> bool { matches!(sku, "book" | "pen") } struct Pick; impl Handle<Shipment> for Pick { fn handle( &self, shipment: &Shipment, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { if shipment.quantity == 0 { tracing::warn!(shipment.id, "an empty shipment rejected"); return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::drop())); } if !in_stock(&shipment.sku) { tracing::info!( shipment.id, shipment.sku, "out of stock, the shipment comes back" ); return ready(Err(HandlerOutcome::retry())); } tracing::info!(shipment.id, shipment.sku, "shipment picked"); ready(Ok(())) } } 处理器的结果 Disposition Broker 做什么 HandlerOutcome::ack() accepted 删除消息 HandlerOutcome::retry() 带 delivery-failed 的 modified 在 delivery-count 中计入这次尝试，并再次投递消息 HandlerOutcome::drop() rejected 执行自己的死信策略 pick 接受已拣选的货件。 空货件永远无法拣选，所以 pick 拒绝它。 Artemis 把被拒绝的消息转入死信地址，默认是 DLQ。 缺货的货件以后也许能拣选，所以 pick 要求再次投递它。 Artemis 在 max-delivery-attempts 次（默认 10 次）之后停止投递一条消息，并把它转入死信地址。

宏 手写 src/main.rs fn service(broker: AmqpBroker) -> RustStream { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("warehouse", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { b.include(pick).max_attempts(nonzero!(5u32)); b.include(log_pick); b.include(restock.batch(nonzero!(20usize))); }) } #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { service(AmqpBroker::new("amqp://artemis:artemis@localhost:5672")) } src/main.rs fn service(broker: AmqpBroker) -> RustStream { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("warehouse", "0.1.0")).with_broker(broker, |b| { let shipments = AmqpAddress::queue("shipments").credit(nonzero!(32)); b.include(subscriber(shipments, Pick).build()) .max_attempts(nonzero!(5u32)); let pick_log = AmqpAddress::queue("pick-log").settle(Settle::AtMostOnce); b.include(subscriber(pick_log, LogPick).build()); let restock = AmqpAddress::queue("restock").batch_wait(Duration::from_millis(50)); b.include( subscriber(restock, Restocking) .batch(nonzero!(20usize)) .build(), ); }) } fn app() -> impl App { service(AmqpBroker::new("amqp://artemis:artemis@localhost:5672")) } fn main() -> ExitCode { run_main(app) } max_attempts 把一个货件的投递次数限定为五次，第一次也算在内。 第五次投递被拒绝，而不是再要求一次。 消息带有 AMQP header 段时，计数就是 Broker 的 delivery-count。 本 crate 发布的消息不带这个段。 对这样的消息，框架自己统计尝试次数：retry 把一份副本发布回 shipments，消息头里带着重试次数。 重试与死信在此基础上加入死信地址和延迟。
订阅默认是至少一次。 服务停止时尚未结算的投递会回到队列，由下一个消费者取得。 因此处理器可能两次看到同一条消息，它的工作必须能容忍这一点。

宏 手写 src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize)] struct Picked { shipment: u64, } #[subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue("pick-log").settle(Settle::AtMostOnce))] async fn log_pick(picked: &Picked) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(picked.shipment, "pick logged"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Picked { shipment: u64, } struct LogPick; impl Handle<Picked> for LogPick { fn handle( &self, picked: &Picked, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(picked.shipment, "pick logged"); ready(Ok(())) } } Settle::AtMostOnce 在每次投递到达时就结算它。 Broker 交出消息的那一刻就忘掉了它，所以处理器完成前的崩溃会丢失这条消息。 这适合拣选日志：缺一行的代价比让 Broker 再处理一遍要小。 处理器的结果已经没有东西可结算：ack 和 nack 返回 AckError::Unsupported，运行时为每一次记录一条警告。

shipments 上的 .credit(nonzero!(32)) 是链路信用：Broker 在服务结算之前最多可以预先发送多少次投递。 默认值是 DEFAULT_CREDIT，即 256。 一半信用结算之后，客户端重新授予全部信用。 因此慢速处理器会让 Broker 放慢发送，而不是占满服务的内存，队列的其余部分则留在 Broker 上，供其他副本读取。 信用是 NonZeroU32，因为没有信用的链路收不到任何东西：credit(nonzero!(0)) 无法编译。

宏 手写 src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize)] struct Restock { sku: String, quantity: u32, } #[subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue("restock").batch_wait(Duration::from_millis(50)))] async fn restock(items: &[Restock]) -> HandlerOutcome { let units: u32 = items.iter().map(|item| item.quantity).sum(); tracing::info!(lines = items.len(), units, "shelves restocked"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Restock { sku: String, quantity: u32, } struct Restocking; impl Handle<[Restock]> for Restocking { fn handle( &self, items: &[Restock], _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), Vec<HandlerOutcome>>> { let units: u32 = items.iter().map(|item| item.quantity).sum(); tracing::info!(lines = items.len(), units, "shelves restocked"); ready(Ok(())) } } 接收切片的处理器得到一批消息，挂载点上的 .batch(nonzero!(20usize)) 设定批的最大大小。 AMQP 1.0 一次 transfer 一条消息，所以批在客户端上组装。 一批最多包含 20 次投递；如果在时限内没有更多投递到达，就少一些。 batch_wait 是未满的批等待更多投递的时长，这里是 50 毫秒，默认是 10 毫秒。 restock 的结果结算这批中的每一次投递。

生产环境的 Broker 要求 TLS 和凭据，它的运维人员则按名称查找服务。

src/main.rs /// Where the broker is and who the service is, as the deployment provides them. struct Endpoint { url: String, username: String, password: String, } impl Endpoint { fn from_env() -> Self { let read = |name: &str| env::var(name).unwrap_or_default(); Self { url: read("AMQP_URL"), username: read("AMQP_USERNAME"), password: read("AMQP_PASSWORD"), } } } fn broker(endpoint: Endpoint) -> AmqpBroker { AmqpBroker::new(endpoint.url) .sasl(Sasl::plain(endpoint.username, endpoint.password)) .container_id("orders-eu-1") } Cargo.toml [dependencies] ruststream-amqp = { version = "0.7", features = ["rustls"] } 部署环境通过环境变量提供地址和凭据。 amqps:// URL 通过 TLS 连接。 它用主机名或 IPv4 地址指明 Broker：TLS 会用这个名称核对 Broker 的证书。 IPv6 地址无法为 TLS 提供服务器名称，因此用它连接会失败。 TLS 需要两个 feature 之一：rustls 使用 rustls，native-tls 使用平台自带的 TLS。 Sasl::plain 用用户名和密码让服务登录。 这时 URL 中不带凭据。 密码中含有在 URL 里有特殊含义的字符（例如 /、? 或 @）时，可以原样交给 Sasl::plain。 Sasl::anonymous 不带凭据连接，Sasl::external 使用连接在 SASL 之外已经建立的凭据。 在 Azure Service Bus 上，用户名是共享访问策略的名称，密码是它的密钥，见其 AMQP 指南。

服务停止时，由内向外关闭连接：先是各订阅的会话，然后是发布者的链路及其会话，最后是连接本身。 此后使用的发布者会返回 AmqpError::NotConnected 错误，而不是在已关闭的连接上报告成功。 服务的 AsyncAPI 文档写明 Broker 的主机和端口，从不包含凭据。

本指南读取一个工作队列，在主题上广播，为暂时离开的读者保留广播，并向一个地址发布消息。 AMQP 1.0 规定了线上格式，地址的含义则交给 Broker 决定。 因此订阅要说明自己想要什么：AmqpAddress 为每种意图提供一个构造函数，链路把这个意图告诉 Broker。 本页所述内容都在 ActiveMQ Artemis 上验证过，本 crate 的测试也运行在它上面。 示例是一个订单服务。 它从队列中取出订单，并在一个主题上公布每个已接收的订单；账务、审计日志和总账都关注这个主题。

宏 手写 src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize)] struct Order { id: u64, amount_cents: u64, } /// What every service that follows orders hears about a taken order. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "order-events")] struct OrderTaken { order: u64, amount_cents: u64, } #[subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue("orders"), reply)] async fn take_order(order: &Order) -> OrderTaken { tracing::info!(order.id, "order taken"); OrderTaken { order: order.id, amount_cents: order.amount_cents, } } src/main.rs #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Order { id: u64, amount_cents: u64, } /// What every service that follows orders hears about a taken order. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Deserialize, Serialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct OrderTaken { order: u64, amount_cents: u64, } impl OutgoingDestination for OrderTaken { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "order-events"; } impl MessageHeaders for OrderTaken { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for OrderTaken { const NAME: &'static str = "OrderTaken"; } struct TakeOrder; impl Handle<Order, OrderTaken> for TakeOrder { fn handle( &self, order: &Order, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<OrderTaken, HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(order.id, "order taken"); ready(Ok(OrderTaken { order: order.id, amount_cents: order.amount_cents, })) } } AmqpAddress::queue 请求一个队列：链路带上 terminus 能力 queue。 Artemis 随后创建一个任播地址 orders，其后有一个队列。 一个队列的各个消费者相互竞争，每个订单只交给其中一个。 要更快地处理订单，就多运行几个服务副本：每个副本都是 orders 的又一个消费者。 take_order 用一个 OrderTaken 回复每个订单。 OrderTaken 用 #[outgoing(name = "order-events")] 指明自己的地址，所以不带参数的 reply 子句把它发往那里。

宏 手写 src/main.rs #[subscriber(AmqpAddress::topic("order-events"))] async fn bill(event: &OrderTaken) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(event.order, event.amount_cents, "invoice issued"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } #[subscriber(AmqpAddress::topic("order-events"))] async fn audit(event: &OrderTaken) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(event.order, "order recorded"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs struct Bill; impl Handle<OrderTaken> for Bill { fn handle( &self, event: &OrderTaken, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(event.order, event.amount_cents, "invoice issued"); ready(Ok(())) } } struct Audit; impl Handle<OrderTaken> for Audit { fn handle( &self, event: &OrderTaken, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(event.order, "order recorded"); ready(Ok(())) } } AmqpAddress::topic 请求一个主题：链路带上能力 topic。 Artemis 把 order-events 设为组播地址，并为每个订阅各建一个队列。 因此 bill 和 audit 各自收到每个 OrderTaken 的一份副本。 主题订阅与它的链路同生共存。 服务停止期间发布到 order-events 的消息不会为它保留。 不能错过任何消息的读者应读取队列。

宏 手写 src/main.rs /// Reads the queue `ledger` that the operator created on the `order-events` address. #[subscriber(AmqpAddress::raw("order-events::ledger"))] async fn post_to_ledger(event: &OrderTaken) -> HandlerOutcome { tracing::info!(event.order, "order posted to the ledger"); HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs /// Reads the queue `ledger` that the operator created on the `order-events` address. struct PostToLedger; impl Handle<OrderTaken> for PostToLedger { fn handle( &self, event: &OrderTaken, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { tracing::info!(event.order, "order posted to the ledger"); ready(Ok(())) } } 总账必须看到每个订单，包括它停止期间接收的订单。 运维人员在组播地址 order-events 上创建一个持久队列 ledger： docker compose exec artemis /opt/activemq-artemis/bin/artemis queue create \ --user artemis --password artemis --silent \ --name ledger --address order-events --auto-create-address \ --multicast --durable --preserve-on-no-consumers 此后发布到 order-events 的每条消息也会进入 ledger，无论 post_to_ledger 是否在运行。 order-events::ledger 是该队列在 Artemis 中的完全限定名：地址、两个冒号、队列名。 AmqpAddress::raw 按原样发送地址，不带任何能力，因此链路附加到这个队列上。 直接写 #[subscriber("order-events::ledger")] 效果相同。

宏 手写 src/main.rs #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( AmqpBroker::new("amqp://artemis:artemis@localhost:5672"), |b| { b.include(take_order).out_reply(Publish); b.include(bill); b.include(audit); b.include(post_to_ledger); }, ) } src/main.rs fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( AmqpBroker::new("amqp://artemis:artemis@localhost:5672"), |b| { b.include( subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue("orders"), TakeOrder) .reply() .build(), ) .out_reply(Publish); b.include(subscriber(AmqpAddress::topic("order-events"), Bill).build()); b.include(subscriber(AmqpAddress::topic("order-events"), Audit).build()); let ledger = AmqpAddress::raw("order-events::ledger"); b.include(subscriber(ledger, PostToLedger).build()); }, ) } fn main() -> ExitCode { run_main(app) } .out_reply(Publish) 指明回复的发布者，即 prelude 中名为 Publish 的 AmqpPublish。 发布在第一次使用时向回复的地址附加一条发送链路，并一直保留它。 Broker 拒收的消息会让发布返回 AmqpError::PublishNotAccepted 错误。

常见的消息头放在 AMQP 的 properties 段中：content-type、correlation-id、reply-to 和 message-id。 其他所有消息头放在 application-properties 中。 本 crate 发出的消息是普通的 AMQP 消息，因此其他语言的客户端不借助 RustStream 也能读取它。 分区键以 PARTITION_KEY_HEADER 消息头传递，并成为消息的 group-id。 Artemis 用 group-id 实现消息分组：同一组的每条消息都交给队列的同一个消费者。 因此以客户为键的订单在多个副本之间也保持顺序。
其他 Broker 用各自的方式为节点命名，raw 把它们的写法原样传过去。 这些写法见各自的文档： RabbitMQ 4.x、 Azure Service Bus、 ActiveMQ Classic（Amazon MQ 运行的就是它）。

本指南通过 AMQP 1.0 询问另一个服务并等待它的答复，在请求的回复地址上作答，并处理无人应答的请求。 请求-响应是协议的一部分。 请求在 reply-to 中带着回复地址，在 correlation-id 中带着一个 id。 答复发往这个地址，并重复这个 id。 示例是一个应用中的两个服务。 定价服务回答关于价格的询问，订单服务向它询问每个订单的价格。

宏 手写 src/main.rs /// What the orders service asks the pricing service. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)] struct Ask { sku: String, } /// The pricing service's answer, sent to the reply address of the request. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] struct Price { sku: String, cents: u64, } /// The catalogue the pricing service answers from. fn price_of(sku: &str) -> Option<u64> { match sku { "book" => Some(1250), "pen" => Some(150), _ => None, } } #[derive(OutSlot)] #[publishes(Price)] struct Answers; #[subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue("prices.quote"))] async fn quote( ask: &Ask, ctx: &mut Context<'_>, Out(answers): Out<impl Publisher, Answers>, ) -> HandlerOutcome { let Some(reply_to) = ctx.headers().reply_to().map(str::to_owned) else { tracing::warn!(ask.sku, "a question without a reply address dropped"); return HandlerOutcome::drop(); }; let Some(cents) = price_of(&ask.sku) else { tracing::info!(ask.sku, "no price for the item, no answer"); return HandlerOutcome::drop(); }; // The requester matches the answer to its question by the correlation id. let mut headers = HeaderMap::new(); if let Some(correlation_id) = ctx.headers().correlation_id() { headers.insert("correlation-id", correlation_id.to_owned()); } let price = Price { sku: ask.sku.clone(), cents, }; if answers .message(&price) .to(reply_to) .with_headers(headers) .publish() .await .is_err() { return HandlerOutcome::retry(); } HandlerOutcome::ack() } src/main.rs /// What the orders service asks the pricing service. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Ask { sku: String, } /// The pricing service's answer, sent to the reply address of the request. #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Price { sku: String, cents: u64, } impl OutgoingDestination for Price { type Form = CallerName; } impl MessageHeaders for Price { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for Price { const NAME: &'static str = "Price"; } /// The catalogue the pricing service answers from. fn price_of(sku: &str) -> Option<u64> { match sku { "book" => Some(1250), "pen" => Some(150), _ => None, } } struct Answers; impl OutSlot for Answers { const NAME: &'static str = "Answers"; type Destination = Reads; } impl PublishedThrough<Answers> for Price {} struct Quote; impl<Sent> Handle<Ask, (), Outs<(Sent,)>> for Quote where Sent: OutEntry<Answers, Wire: Publisher>, { async fn handle( &self, ask: &Ask, outs: &Outs<(Sent,)>, ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<(), HandlerOutcome> { let Some(reply_to) = ctx.headers().reply_to().map(str::to_owned) else { tracing::warn!(ask.sku, "a question without a reply address dropped"); return Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()); }; let Some(cents) = price_of(&ask.sku) else { tracing::info!(ask.sku, "no price for the item, no answer"); return Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()); }; // The requester matches the answer to its question by the correlation id. let mut headers = HeaderMap::new(); if let Some(correlation_id) = ctx.headers().correlation_id() { headers.insert("correlation-id", correlation_id.to_owned()); } let price = Price { sku: ask.sku.clone(), cents, }; if outs .get(Answers) .message(&price) .to(reply_to) .with_headers(headers) .publish() .await .is_err() { return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()); } Ok(()) } } 请求到达应答方时，reply-to 消息头中带着它的回复地址，ctx.headers().reply_to() 读取这个地址。 quote 通过它的 Answers 槽位用 to(reply_to) 发布价格，因为每个请求的地址都不同。 因此 Price 不声明自己的地址。 答复带着请求的 correlation-id，请求方只接收 id 相符的答复。 没有价格的商品得不到答复，请求方的超时结束等待。 应答方读取队列 prices.quote。 定价服务的每个副本都是它的又一个消费者，每个请求只交给其中一个。

宏 手写 src/main.rs /// How long the orders service waits for a price. const PRICING_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2); /// How long an order waits before it asks for its price again. const RETRY_DELAY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30); #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "orders")] struct Order { id: u64, sku: String, } #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] #[outgoing(name = "orders.priced")] struct Priced { order: u64, cents: u64, } #[derive(OutSlot)] struct Pricing; #[subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue("orders"), reply)] async fn price_order( order: &Order, Out(pricing): Out<impl RequestReply, Pricing>, ) -> Result<Priced, HandlerOutcome> { let Ok(ask) = serde_json::to_vec(&Ask { sku: order.sku.clone(), }) else { return Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()); }; let request = OutgoingMessage::new("prices.quote", ask.as_slice()); let reply = match pricing.request(request, PRICING_TIMEOUT).await { Ok(reply) => reply, Err(err) => { tracing::warn!(order.id, %err, "no price, the order asks again later"); return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RETRY_DELAY)); } }; let Ok(price) = serde_json::from_slice::<Price>(reply.payload()) else { return Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()); }; tracing::info!(order.id, price.cents, "order priced"); Ok(Priced { order: order.id, cents: price.cents, }) } src/main.rs /// How long the orders service waits for a price. const PRICING_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2); /// How long an order waits before it asks for its price again. const RETRY_DELAY: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30); #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Order { id: u64, sku: String, } impl OutgoingDestination for Order { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "orders"; } impl MessageHeaders for Order { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for Order { const NAME: &'static str = "Order"; } #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Priced { order: u64, cents: u64, } impl OutgoingDestination for Priced { type Form = FixedName; const DESTINATION: &'static str = "orders.priced"; } impl MessageHeaders for Priced { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for Priced { const NAME: &'static str = "Priced"; } struct Pricing; impl OutSlot for Pricing { const NAME: &'static str = "Pricing"; type Destination = Reads; } struct PriceOrder; impl<Asks> Handle<Order, Priced, Outs<(Asks,)>> for PriceOrder where Asks: OutEntry<Pricing, Wire: RequestReply>, { async fn handle( &self, order: &Order, outs: &Outs<(Asks,)>, _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> Result<Priced, HandlerOutcome> { let Ok(ask) = serde_json::to_vec(&Ask { sku: order.sku.clone(), }) else { return Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()); }; let request = OutgoingMessage::new("prices.quote", ask.as_slice()); let reply = match outs.get(Pricing).request(request, PRICING_TIMEOUT).await { Ok(reply) => reply, Err(err) => { tracing::warn!(order.id, %err, "no price, the order asks again later"); return Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(RETRY_DELAY)); } }; let Ok(price) = serde_json::from_slice::<Price>(reply.payload()) else { return Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()); }; tracing::info!(order.id, price.cents, "order priced"); Ok(Priced { order: order.id, cents: price.cents, }) } } price_order 读取订单，并在 prices.quote 上询问每个订单的价格。 Pricing 槽位的约束是 Out<impl RequestReply, _>：函数体声明它需要请求-响应，而不指明 Broker。 应用把这个槽位与普通的 Publish 策略配对，该策略的发布者 AmqpPublisher 支持请求-响应。 request 附加一条动态接收链路，于是 Broker 为这一个请求创建一个私有的回复地址。 它发布问题，设置好 reply-to 和 correlation-id，并以第一个相符的答复完成。 ActiveMQ Artemis 用一个临时队列支撑动态链路。 问题是一条原始消息，所以函数体自己编码问题并解码答复，这里用的是 serde_json。 价格得知后，订单的回复 Priced 随即发出。 无人应答的请求在超时（这里是两秒）后返回 AmqpError::RequestTimeout 错误。 无论哪种情况，回复链路都会被分离。 订单随后在队列中等待 30 秒，再询问一次。

宏 手写 src/main.rs #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( AmqpBroker::new("amqp://artemis:artemis@localhost:5672"), |b| { b.include(quote).out(Answers, Publish).build(); b.include(price_order) .out_reply(Publish) .out(Pricing, Publish) .build(); }, ) } src/main.rs fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("orders", "0.1.0")).with_broker( AmqpBroker::new("amqp://artemis:artemis@localhost:5672"), |b| { b.include(subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue("prices.quote"), Quote).build()) .out(Answers, Publish) .build(); b.include( subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue("orders"), PriceOrder) .reply() .build(), ) .out_reply(Publish) .out(Pricing, Publish) .build(); }, ) } fn main() -> ExitCode { run_main(app) } 两个槽位都使用普通的 Publish 策略：一个发布答复，另一个提出问题。 发起对话的请求没有要回复的投递。 它从启动钩子 b.after_startup(Publish, ..) 中运行，在交给钩子的发布者上调用 request。 示例文件中的测试在一个进程内应用中运行这两半。 进程内 Broker 把请求路由到应用自己的应答方，按关联 id 匹配答复，并让沉默的应答方超时。
本指南立即或稍后重试一次投递，限定尝试次数，把一直失败的消息转入死信地址，并标记副本。 AMQP 1.0 没有延迟重新投递，链路也无法声明投递上限或死信地址。 这两件事都由框架来做：挂载点声明上限和死信地址，延迟重试以消息副本的形式发出，消息头里带着重试次数。 示例是一个退款服务，它通过发卡处理商发出退款。

处理商有三种拒绝退款的方式，每种需要不同的结果。 Busy 表示它暂时不再受理大额退款：立即重试仍会被拒绝，所以 retry_after 等待 30 秒。 Unavailable 表示发卡银行没有应答：retry 立即再试一次。 Declined 表示卡账户已经关闭，再试一次也是同样的答复，所以这笔退款被丢弃。 宏 手写 src/main.rs /// How long a busy processor asks its callers to wait. const BACKOFF: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30); #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, Outgoing)] struct Refund { id: u64, card: String, amount_cents: u64, } #[subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue("refunds"))] async fn process_refund(refund: &Refund) -> HandlerOutcome { match send_refund(refund) { Ok(()) => HandlerOutcome::ack(), // Past the rate limit: a delivery right now would be refused again. Err(Refusal::Busy) => HandlerOutcome::retry_after(BACKOFF), // No answer: try again at once, up to the attempt cap. Err(Refusal::Unavailable) => HandlerOutcome::retry(), Err(Refusal::Declined) => { tracing::warn!(refund.id, "card declined, refund dropped"); HandlerOutcome::drop() } } } src/main.rs /// How long a busy processor asks its callers to wait. const BACKOFF: Duration = Duration::from_secs(30); #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)] #[schemars(crate = "ruststream::schemars")] struct Refund { id: u64, card: String, amount_cents: u64, } impl OutgoingDestination for Refund { type Form = CallerName; } impl MessageHeaders for Refund { type Contract = NoHeaders; } impl MessageInfo for Refund { const NAME: &'static str = "Refund"; } struct ProcessRefund; impl Handle<Refund> for ProcessRefund { fn handle( &self, refund: &Refund, _outs: &(), _ctx: &mut Context<'_>, ) -> impl Future<Output = Result<(), HandlerOutcome>> { ready(match send_refund(refund) { Ok(()) => Ok(()), // Past the rate limit: a delivery right now would be refused again. Err(Refusal::Busy) => Err(HandlerOutcome::retry_after(BACKOFF)), // No answer: try again at once, up to the attempt cap. Err(Refusal::Unavailable) => Err(HandlerOutcome::retry()), Err(Refusal::Declined) => { tracing::warn!(refund.id, "card declined, refund dropped"); Err(HandlerOutcome::drop()) } }) } } retry_after 结算这次投递，并在延迟过去后把一份副本发布到 refunds。 副本带着重试次数消息头（RETRY_COUNT_HEADER），其值加一。 延迟的副本是至多一次的：在延迟结束前停止的进程会丢失它。 在队列上，副本像其他消息一样交给一个消费者。

宏 手写 src/main.rs #[ruststream::app] fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("refunds", "0.1.0")).with_broker( AmqpBroker::new("amqp://artemis:artemis@localhost:5672"), |b| { // Five deliveries of one refund, the first included; then the dead-letter address. b.include(process_refund) .max_attempts(nonzero!(5u32)) .dead_letter("refunds.dead") .out_retry(Publish) .transform(Retried); b.include(review); }, ) } src/main.rs fn app() -> impl App { RustStream::new(AppInfo::new("refunds", "0.1.0")).with_broker( AmqpBroker::new("amqp://artemis:artemis@localhost:5672"), |b| { // Five deliveries of one refund, the first included; then the dead-letter address. b.include(subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue("refunds"), ProcessRefund).build()) .max_attempts(nonzero!(5u32)) .dead_letter("refunds.dead") .out_retry(Publish) .transform(Retried); b.include(subscriber(AmqpAddress::queue("refunds.dead"), Review).build()); }, ) } fn main() -> ExitCode { run_main(app) } max_attempts 统计一笔退款的每次投递，第一次也算在内。 第五次投递不再重试：dead_letter 把它按到达时的载荷和消息头原样发布到 refunds.dead。 被丢弃的退款会被拒绝，由 Broker 自己的死信策略处理，而不是进入 refunds.dead。 在声明了上限时，框架从投递中读取计数。 消息带有 AMQP header 段时，计数就是 Broker 的 delivery-count。 本 crate 发布的消息不带这个段，所以这时 retry 会立即发布一份副本，由重试次数消息头统计尝试次数。 有上限而没有 dead_letter 时，最后一次投递会被拒绝，由 Broker 的死信策略决定去向。 Broker 也有自己的上限：Artemis 在 max-delivery-attempts 次（默认 10 次）之后停止投递。 上限只应由一方负责：低于 Broker 上限的上限会让框架的计数生效。

副本发布到订阅自己的地址。 在主题地址上，这个地址是共用的，所以主题上的每个订阅都会收到副本，而不只是要求重试的那一个。 消息只归一个读者所有时，在队列上重试。
